content_voiceover: This slide is a critical technical caveat about the DAT that gets tested on boards. The standard polyspecific direct antiglobulin test can only detect IgG and C3d, that's it, nothing else. Look at the gel card image, the polyspecific reagent shows positive reactions only in the IgG lane and the C3d lane, the IgA and IgM lanes are negative even when those immunoglobulins may be present, because the reagent simply isn't built to catch them. This matters clinically because some AIHA cases are mediated by IgA or IgM alone, and those cases can have a falsely negative or incomplete-looking polyspecific DAT, a classic pitfall, DAT-negative AIHA. When the polyspecific DAT is positive, or when you have high clinical suspicion despite a negative polyspecific test, you escalate to the monospecific direct antiglobulin test, shown in the bottom panel, where you add specific antibodies against each individual component: IgG, IgA, IgM, C3c, C3d, and a control. This lets you determine exactly which immunoglobulin class or complement component is coating the red cells, which in turn narrows the differential, for example IgG-plus-C3d suggests warm AIHA, while C3d alone suggests cold agglutinin disease or PCH. So the workflow is polyspecific DAT to screen, monospecific DAT to characterize.
keypoints: Standard polyspecific DAT detects ONLY IgG and C3d — misses IgA, IgM alone
IgA- or IgM-mediated AIHA can have a falsely negative/unrevealing polyspecific DAT
Monospecific DAT adds individual antisera (IgG, IgA, IgM, C3c, C3d) to pinpoint the coating protein
Monospecific pattern narrows diagnosis: IgG±C3d → warm AIHA; C3d alone → CAD/PCH
keypoint_voiceover: Know this limitation cold, the standard polyspecific direct antiglobulin test only detects IgG and C3d, it cannot pick up IgA or IgM even if they're coating the red cells. That means rare IgA- or IgM-mediated AIHA can look falsely negative on a routine DAT. When you need more detail, or when the standard DAT doesn't explain the clinical picture, you run the monospecific DAT, testing individually for IgG, IgA, IgM, C3c, and C3d, which tells you precisely what's coating the cells and helps distinguish warm AIHA from cold agglutinin disease or paroxysmal cold hemoglobinuria.
